reason: The PR changes active CP propagation in PropXplusYeqZ and PropAbsolute: it chooses range versus arc-consistency filtering from current domain structure and removes intervals in bulk outside LCG. These changes can alter propagation work and the search tree, beyond a local formatting or build change.
solver_behavior_hypothesis: Dynamic domain structure may avoid expensive arc-consistency scans or repeated value removals while preserving all valid integer-domain deductions. Different deductions may change downstream search and exact proof time.
causal_chain: PropXplusYeqZ now treats fixed or bounded variables as range-only when enough operands qualify and checks whether the domain product is below the arc-consistency threshold. PropAbsolute uses interval removal when LCG explanations are unnecessary. Both alter propagation events and possible branching trajectories.
structural_trigger: Integer CP models with active x+y=z or absolute-value constraints, mixed enumerated and bounded domains, and enough propagation events to reach both the range-only and arc-consistency branches; models without those constraints are controls.
activation_probe: Count calls and domain-shape decisions in both propagators, arc-consistency versus range filtering, interval versus per-value removals, contradictions, nodes, and inactive paths on paired pinned builds.
instance_selection_rule: Freeze additive and absolute-value CP model families by domain representation, variable count, and difficulty before hidden scoring; include a nontriggering CP control and retain all selected cases, seeds, and timeouts.
workload_exposure_plan: Use the shared Choco driver with original-model independent solution checks. Add a configuration-backed arithmetic CP panel only if source-level traces prove the changed propagators execute; ordinary bin-packing or coloring activity alone cannot qualify this PR.
mathematical_risk: A wrong range-only decision or interval deletion can remove feasible integer assignments, miss a contradiction, or make an invalid optimality or infeasibility claim; LCG explanation handling must remain valid.
independent_check_plan: Check every returned assignment against original additive and absolute-value constraints and objective values; compare optimal and infeasible claims with independent exact proofs on tractable cases, and run targeted propagation regressions for enumerated and bounded domains.
hidden_generalization_plan: Evaluate paired held-out arithmetic CP instances across domain structures and sizes at fixed CPU budgets and seeds, with per-family solved coverage, proof time, valid incumbent quality, and regression accounting.
overlap_review: Adjacent Choco PR #1152 targets decision-path overhead at a different pre-PR commit. This PR is one propagation change bundle and must not be split into separate tasks solely by its two propagators or test seeds.
resource_risk: Bulk removal may increase explanation or allocation work under LCG, and a weaker filtering choice can enlarge the search tree even if a propagation call gets faster.
